name: Static Website
description: A pattern for delivering informational content through pre-rendered static pages served from a CDN or object storage. Suitable for public-facing informational services, campaign sites, and documentation portals where content changes infrequently and no server-side processing is required.
whenToUse: Public informational services with no user authentication or personalisation
Campaign or promotional microsites with a defined lifespan
Documentation portals or knowledge bases with infrequent content updates
Services where maximum availability and minimal operational overhead are priorities
Content-heavy sites where page load performance is critical for accessibility
whenNotToUse: Services requiring user authentication or session management
Applications needing real-time data or dynamic content generation
Transactional services where users submit forms or make payments
Services requiring server-side business logic or database queries
Platforms needing personalised content based on user roles or preferences

typicalComponents.name: Static Site Generator
typicalComponents.purpose: Compile content into pre-rendered HTML pages at build time

typicalComponents.name: Content Delivery Network
typicalComponents.purpose: Distribute static assets globally with low-latency edge caching
typicalComponents.technology: CloudFront, Azure CDN, or Cloud CDN

typicalComponents.name: Object Storage
typicalComponents.purpose: Store and serve static HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and media files
typicalComponents.technology: S3, Azure Blob Storage, or Cloud Storage

typicalComponents.name: DNS Management
typicalComponents.purpose: Route traffic to CDN distribution with health checks
typicalComponents.technology: Route 53, Azure DNS, or Cloud DNS

typicalComponents.name: CI/CD Pipeline
typicalComponents.purpose: Automate build and deployment of static content on commit
typicalComponents.technology: GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or Cloud Build

securityControls: Enforce HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ and HSTS headers on all responses
Implement Content Security Policy headers to prevent XSS and injection attacks
Configure WAF rules to block common attack patterns and bot traffic
Use signed URLs or origin access identity to prevent direct bucket access
Enable access logging on CDN and storage for audit trail
Implement Subresource Integrity for third-party scripts
resilienceConsiderations: CDN provides inherent multi-region redundancy through edge caching
Object storage offers 99.999999999% durability with cross-region replication
No server-side components means no single point of failure for compute
Implement cache invalidation strategy for content updates
Configure custom error pages for graceful degradation
costConsiderations: Extremely low running costs — primarily storage and data transfer charges
No compute costs as there are no servers to maintain
CDN costs scale linearly with traffic but remain low for typical government sites
Build pipeline costs are minimal and only incurred during deployments
Cost-effective for high-traffic sites due to edge caching reducing origin requests
operationalConsiderations: Minimal operational overhead — no servers to patch or scale
Content updates require a build and deploy cycle rather than direct editing
Monitoring focuses on CDN metrics, cache hit ratios, and availability
No on-call requirements for compute infrastructure
Content authors may need training on static site generator workflows

questionsToAsk: How frequently will content be updated and who will be responsible for updates?
Is there a requirement for content preview or staging before publication?
Are there accessibility requirements beyond WCAG 2.1 AA compliance?
Will the site need to support multiple languages or locales?
What is the expected traffic volume and are there known peak periods?
Is there a requirement for search functionality within the static content?
commonMistakes: Using a static site pattern when the service actually requires user interaction or form submissions
Not implementing proper cache invalidation leading to stale content after updates
Exposing the origin storage bucket directly without CDN protection
Neglecting to set appropriate security headers on CDN responses
Over-engineering the build pipeline for what should be a simple content deployment
